run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Runbook fetched: skill_id=database-troubleshooting (Database Connection Troubleshooting). Step-by-step result: (1) Application status - checked; Deployment app-94/blue-whale has 1/1 ready replicas and its only pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-dmnbj is Running, ready with restartCount 0, and all 6 events in the window are Normal rollout events at 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet), with no FailedMount/Unhealthy/Evicted/OOM event. (2) Application logs - attempted; fetch_pod_logs returned no_data with 0 lines read from container blue-whale and no previous container instance, so no timeout/connection error text could be observed. (3) Database Service and endpoints - checked; Service app-94/postgres exists (ClusterIP 10.96.25.89, port 5432 -> targetPort 5432, selector app=postgres-db), but its Endpoints object 'postgres' in app-94 has subsets: null, i.e. zero addresses, while app-94/blue-whale endpoints list 10.244.0.40:8080. (4) Connectivity test - could not be carried out: no exec/network-probe tool is available. (5) Database health - could not be carried out: no postgres pod exists anywhere (33 pods cluster-wide, none postgres), no postgres Deployment among the 25 deployments, and the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager. (6) Connection-pool config - checked; container is python:3.9-slim running python /app/app.py with DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20, memory limit 128Mi, app code from Secret volume blue-whale-app. Other candidates checked and not supported: zero NetworkPolicies and zero ResourceQuotas cluster-wide, and no pod crash/OOM evidence. The observable fault is therefore a database name that resolves to a Service with no backing endpoint: Service app-94/postgres selects app=postgres-db but no such pod or workload exists. The blue-whale-side timeout evidence itself is unverified: its logs were empty, and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE during this Run, so its error rate, latency and traces could not be read, and I do not assert its own error spans or error log lines. Change history is not integrated, so whether a postgres workload existed earlier and was removed is unknown.

claims.text: Deployment app-94/blue-whale (metadata.generation 1, created 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z, managed by kubectl-client-side-apply) runs container blue-whale from image python:3.9-slim with command [python /app/app.py] and env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20; app code is mounted at /app from Secret blue-whale-app and memory limit is 128Mi.

The only pod in namespace app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-dmnbj, owned by ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5, phase Running, container blue-whale ready=true, restartCount 0, empty lastState, startTime 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z; namespace app-94 itself was created 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z.

Service app-94/postgres exists with selector app=postgres-db, ClusterIP 10.96.25.89 and port 5432 -> targetPort 5432, and the matching Endpoints object 'postgres' in app-94 returned subsets: null (no addresses), whereas Endpoints 'blue-whale' in app-94 lists address 10.244.0.40 (pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-dmnbj) on port 8080.

No database workload backs that Service: the cluster-wide pod list contains 33 pods and none is a postgres pod (the only app-94 pod is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-dmnbj), the cluster-wide deployment list contains 25 deployments and none is named postgres or selects app=postgres-db, and the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager.

All 6 Kubernetes events in the authorized window are Normal events for the blue-whale rollout in app-94 at 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 0->1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started); no warning-type event such as FailedMount, Unhealthy, Evicted or OOMKilling was returned.
Namespace app-94 holds only one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt; no application configuration ConfigMap exists there, so no fault-injection setting was found in app-94 configuration.

The most likely cause of database connection timeouts for blue-whale is that DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local resolves to Service app-94/postgres, which has no backing endpoints because no pod labelled app=postgres-db (or any postgres workload) exists in the cluster; every connection attempt on port 5432 therefore has no destination.

Pod-level failure of blue-whale (crash, OOMKill, probe failure or unhealthy container) is not the cause of the reported timeouts: the pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and no Unhealthy/Evicted/OOMKilling event exists in the window.

NetworkPolicy blocking egress from blue-whale to postgres is not supported: the cluster has zero NetworkPolicy objects and zero ResourceQuota objects, so neither can be blocking or limiting the database path.

Deploy or restore the missing postgres backing workload for namespace app-94 (a Deployment/StatefulSet with pods labelled app=postgres-db exposing port 5432) and verify Endpoints 'postgres' in app-94 becomes non-empty; if the database is intentionally external, change DB_HOST on Deployment app-94/blue-whale to the real host instead of the dangling Service name.

gaps: blue-whale's own timeout/error text was not observed: fetch_pod_logs for app-94/blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-dmnbj returned no_data (view 45a911cc-a032-4175-b449-9105ab7cd420-t0:9ee9f496-48fe-41f1-8dab-c1436384a0e4, 0 lines read, no previous container instance), so the application-side error signal is unverified.
A later repeat log read (view 66da4d8f-efed-4514-be4e-5bc7017beefe-t1:ab142416-9c33-42e7-8440-a5d4eab81346) also returned no_data with 0 lines.

A pod query filtering labels app=postgres-db / opentelemetry.io/name=postgres returned no_data (view 4e09d73a-f7f6-4558-a017-039075900103-t2:5697778e-a1f2-467c-a580-d8885e2ace2b): that query matched nothing, so absence of a postgres pod is shown by the complete cluster-wide pod list, not by this filtered query alone.

All Prometheus queries returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules), so error-rate, latency, rpc/http server metrics and kube-state-metrics series for blue-whale and any database could not be checked; those readings are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable too (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace evidence for blue-whale or a database dependency could be obtained.

Runbook step 4 (in-pod connectivity test to postgres:5432) could not be carried out: no exec/network-probe tool is available. Runbook step 5 (database health / psql check) could not be carried out because no database pod exists to connect to.

Whether a postgres workload previously existed in app-94 and was deleted or scaled to 0 cannot be determined: the change_history integration is not integrated, namespace app-94 was itself created at 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z, and only 6 events (all timestamped 2026-11-23T16:39:40Z) were retained in the window.
Contents of Secret blue-whale-app (which supplies /app/app.py) cannot be read, so the application's connection logic and pool behaviour could not be verified.

The exact client-side error class (timeout versus connection refused) for blue-whale's connections to the empty postgres Service is unknown; no client-side log, metric or trace was available to distinguish them.
next_steps: Create or restore the postgres workload for app-94 with pods labelled app=postgres-db on port 5432, then confirm Endpoints object 'postgres' in app-94 lists addresses.
If the database is meant to be external to the cluster, correct DB_HOST in the app-94/blue-whale Deployment (currently postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local) instead of relying on the empty Service.
Once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable again, check blue-whale's error rate/latency and any database client spans to confirm the timeout symptom and close the evidence gap.
Confirm with the platform owner whether a postgres Deployment for app-94 ever existed (change history is not integrated in this Run).
